t: A servo axis on a Festo FHPP drive
html:
Everything so far moved on a contactor or a VFD: a belt runs or it does not, faster or slower. A servo axis is the other kind of motion. The PLC names a position and the drive puts the carriage there, to a hundredth of a millimetre, and tells you when it has arrived. the palette has a Drives & Axes category (the VFD of the case packer chapter moved there too) with a Linear Axis part. Three things make a servo axis, and it pays to keep them apart: the axis is the mechanics, a toothed-belt or spindle profile with a carriage; the servo motor is bolted to its end; the drive is the servo controller, a box in the cabinet. The part on the floor is the axis with its motor. The drive is the module in I/O Configuration, and the PLC talks to it over EtherNet/IP with Festo’s FHPP profile, the Festo Handling and Positioning Profile. This chapter builds the small panel that drives it and walks the handshake rung by rung. Level 13 (chapter 45) puts the axis to work.

What FHPP is

A Festo drive on EtherNet/IP exchanges eight bytes each way on the implicit connection, and FHPP says what the bytes mean. The PLC writes two control bytes, CCON and CPOS, a record number, a velocity and a position; the drive answers with two status bytes, SCON and SPOS, the record it ran, a fourth byte (the actual velocity in Direct mode, the record status byte in Record Select) and its actual position, in hundredths of a millimetre unless the drive is scaled otherwise. A real CMMT is scaled in Festo Automation Suite; the axis module’s Position unit on the bus (0.1, 0.01 or 0.001 mm, in the axis’s properties) is set to match it. Logix Connect gives every bit a name under the module, so the rungs read Axis1:O.Enable and Axis1:I.Motion_Complete rather than Axis1:O.Data[0].0; the bit map underneath is the profile’s.

The part and its module

Place a Linear Axis and press Add Axis Module in its properties: a module Axis1 appears in I/O Configuration with the FHPP members, and the axis is tied to it. The part has no wired signals at all; it moves on the module’s tags, which is exactly how the real one works. Its properties are the axis you ordered: Axis size (Festo builds them in profile sizes, 45 to 185 mm wide, toothed belt or ball-screw spindle; the size sets the drawn width, the stroke range and the drive’s velocity and acceleration ceiling, and a setting past the ceiling is held at it), Stroke in millimetres, the maximum velocity that 100 % in a record means, the acceleration, the homing and jog speeds, and the records: a position and a velocity percentage each, 200@50, 1000@80, 1800@100 here. On a live module the part follows the real drive’s Actual_Pos instead.

The program, top down

File → New Project → Sandbox: servo axis opens the panel with these seven rungs. Read them in order: power, fault handling, homing, the record, the start, the handshake.

Reading the drive: the control and status bits, and what a healthy one looks like

Two things about FHPP trip up everybody the first time, and they are the same thing seen from both ends. On the way out, the bits named Stop and Halt are permissions, not commands: a 1 means allowed, a 0 means stop or hold. On the way back, the drive answers every permission with an acknowledge bit that mirrors it, so a healthy, idle drive shows a row of 1s where you might expect 0s. Learn the idle picture once and every fault afterwards is a bit that is not where it should be.

The Power rung

XIC(Run) [OTE(Axis1:O.Enable),OTE(Axis1:O.Stop),OTE(Axis1:O.Halt),OTE(Lamp_Run)]; HOW THIS RUNG WORKS In words. When Run is on, the rung turns Axis1:O.Enable on (and off again whenever the rung is false), turns Axis1:O.Stop on (and off again whenever the rung is false), turns Axis1:O.Halt on (and off again whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Run on (and off again whenever the rung is false). Left to right: 1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on. 2. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work. Path 1 1. OTE(Axis1:O.Enable) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Enable on (and off again whenever the rung is false). Path 2 1. OTE(Axis1:O.Stop) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Stop on (and off again whenever the rung is false). Path 3 1. OTE(Axis1:O.Halt) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Halt on (and off again whenever the rung is false). Path 4 1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off again whenever the rung is false).

When Run is true all three drive bits go to 1 and the drive reads them as:

OutputFHPP bit1 means0 means
Axis1:O.EnableCCON.0 ENABLEPower stage on: the motor is under closed-loop control and holds positionDisabled: no torque, no commands taken; a running move coasts to a controlled stop and the task is dropped
Axis1:O.StopCCON.1 STOPOperation enabled, despite the name. The drive’s "OK to run"Controlled stop on the stop ramp; the task is cancelled; no Start is taken until the bit is 1 again
Axis1:O.HaltCPOS.0 HALTNot halted: a move runsThe move pauses on its ramp but the task is kept; raise Halt and a Start resumes to the same target. The sandbox panel’s Hold button works this bit

The drive sequences them itself, Enable → Stop → Halt, so writing all three in one rung is normal; when the last one is in it answers with Op_Enabled, and that is the bit the Home and Start rungs wait on. Stop throws a move away; Halt parks it. That is the whole difference, and it decides what you tie each bit to. Tying all three to Run, as above, means a Stop button or an E-stop cancels the move and takes the torque off: fine for a pick-and-place. On a machine that should hold position on a stop, keep Enable on and drop only Stop; the axis stands still under torque and the next Start begins a fresh move.

A healthy drive, idle and homed

This is the axis in the sandbox scene after Axis_On and a Home, standing at 0 with nothing to do. Every bit in both tables is in the state it should be; the two rows of 1s on the status side are the acknowledges.

InputFHPP bitHealthyWhat it tells you
EnabledSCON.0 ENABLED1The power stage is on: your Enable was accepted
Op_EnabledSCON.1 OPEN1All three permissions are in; the drive will take Home, Start, Jog. Everything downstream waits on this
WarningSCON.2 WARN0A command was ignored (a Start while moving, a Start with Halt low). Not a fault: the drive carries on, and Reset clears it
FaultSCON.3 FAULT0Faulted: Op_Enabled drops, the axis stops, nothing runs until the rising edge of Reset
InputFHPP bitHealthy idleWhat it tells you
Load_VoltageSCON.4 VLOAD1The motor supply is present. Separate from the 24 V logic supply: on a real panel this is the bit that goes to 0 when the safety contactor drops the motor power while the drive stays awake
FCT_ControlSCON.5 FCT/MMI0The PLC has control. When a technician takes device control from the Festo Configuration Tool this goes to 1 and your Starts are ignored; Lock (CCON.5) refuses it
OPM1_Ack, OPM2_AckSCON.6, SCON.70, 0The operating mode the drive is actually in: 0 0 is Record Select, 1 0 is Direct mode. They mirror your OPM1 and OPM2; check them before a Start if you switch modes
Halt_AckSPOS.0 HALT1Mirrors Halt: 1 = not halted, free to move
Start_AckSPOS.1 ACK01 while your Start is high and the drive has taken it. The edge the unlatch rung uses; a refused Start gets a fault instead, which is why the unlatch rung has a Fault branch too
Motion_CompleteSPOS.2 MC1No task in progress. Drops the instant a move or a homing starts, returns when the target is reached. Gate your in-position logic on it
Teach_AckSPOS.3 TEACH01 after a Teach stored the position
MovingSPOS.4 MOV0The axis is in motion; use it to keep a second Start out
Drag_ErrorSPOS.5 DEV0Following error: the axis is not where the drive commanded, a mechanical problem or an overload
StandstillSPOS.6 STILL1At rest with operation enabled; off while moving
ReferencedSPOS.7 REF1Homed. 0 after power-up (and after a homing starts) until the reference run completes; a Start with this 0 is the positioning- before-homing fault
Record_No,

Actual_Posbytes 3, 4, 5- 8last record, 0, positionThe record that ran; byte 4 is the speed in percent in Direct mode and the record status byte in Record Select (0 here: no record chaining); the position in the module’s unit, 0.01 mm unless set otherwise: 150000 is 1500 mm

The LEDs on the motor

The drive’s status is also on the machine, where a technician sees it without a laptop: four LEDs on the motor end of the axis. They are the four status bits that matter most, and the healthy idle picture is three lit and one dark.

LEDColourStatus bitLit means
ENgreenOp_Enabled (SCON.1)The drive is enabled and in operation: Enable, Stop and Halt are all 1. Dark with Axis_On on: look at the Power rung’s conditions, or ERR is lit
REFblueReferenced (SPOS.7)The axis is homed; positioning is allowed. Dark: Home has not run yet (or is running), and a Start will fault
MCyellowMotion_Complete and not MovingAt rest with the last task finished. Dark while a move or a homing runs; back when the target is reached
ERRredFault (SCON.3)Faulted: EN goes dark with it, the axis stops, nothing runs until Reset. The log names the fault

Read them as a pattern. EN REF MC: healthy and idle, ready for a Start. EN alone: powered but not homed, the state right after power-up. EN REF with MC dark: moving. REF MC with EN dark: Axis_On is off, or Stop or Halt has dropped: the drive remembers it is homed, it just will not move. ERR: Reset, then see which of the others comes back. Nothing lit: no power to the drive, or the module is not connected (Axis1 red in I/O Configuration).

Auto-home

XIC(Run)XIC(Axis1:I.Op_Enabled)XIO(Axis1:I.Referenced)XIO(Axis1:I.Moving)XIO(Ax is1:I.Fault)OTE(Axis1:O.Home); PREDICT IT · 5 Run is on, Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on, Axis1:I.Referenced is off, Axis1:I.Moving is off and Axis1:I.Fault is on. What does the rung do? Work it out from the rung before you read on. The answer is at the end of this chapter. HOW THIS RUNG WORKS In words. When Run is on, Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on, Axis1:I.Referenced is off, Axis1:I.Moving is off and Axis1:I.Fault is off, the rung turns Axis1:O.Home on (and off again whenever the rung is false). Left to right: 1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on. 2. XIC(Axis1:I.Op_Enabled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on. 3. XIO(Axis1:I.Referenced) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Referenced is off. 4. XIO(Axis1:I.Moving) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Moving is off. 5. XIO(Axis1:I.Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Fault is off. 6. OTE(Axis1:O.Home) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Home on (and off again whenever the rung is false).

The lesson programs home from a button so the fault can be shown on purpose; a cell that runs on its own homes itself like this. The instant the drive is in operation and the axis is not referenced, Home goes true; the drive takes the rising edge and runs its reference move; Referenced comes on and the XIO opens. Two details that make it right: XIO(Moving) opens as soon as homing starts, so Home is a short pulse rather than held for the whole run, which is fine because HOM is edge-triggered and dropping it does not abort the homing; and XIO(Fault) means a faulted drive is never asked to home, but since Referenced is still 0 it homes again by itself the moment Reset clears the fault. Where the homing goes is not in the program at all: the method, to a reference switch, to the end stop with a current limit, or switch then index, is configured in the drive. With an absolute multiturn encoder there is no homing run and Referenced is 1 from power-up.

Field notes: the first program, and what went wrong

This section is the log of one afternoon spent writing the Level 13 program and the guided track from scratch, kept because every item in it is a mistake the next person will make too. Each is a symptom, the cause, and the fix. Going through a program this way, one failure at a time, is what makes it bulletproof: a rung you have watched fail is a rung you understand.

Every Go faults, and the fault lamp is on

Where to read it: the axis itself says FAULT: not referenced, Home first under the carriage, and the Simulator Log tab (bottom of the window; on the phone, Output → Simulator Log) has the full line: Axis1: fault: positioning before homing (axis not referenced): pulse Home first. The simulated drive raises exactly three faults: a Start before the axis is referenced; a Start for a record that is not set (record 3 is not set (records 1 to 2)); a target past the stroke. Everything else the drive refuses is a warning, not a fault: a Start while moving (a double start), a Start with Halt low. A warning sets the Warning bit and a log line, the axis carries on, Reset clears it. A fault drops Op_Enabled and stops the axis until Reset. The cause, that afternoon: the Home rung had been typed with the controller in Run. It was a pending online edit, verified and visible and not running. See the Watch-for above; the card now says so, and Program → Run (a download) or the card’s Assemble button makes it the program.

The carriage is stranded over a bin

Clear Parts removed the bottle the gripper was holding; the set-down rung, which is what sent the carriage back to the pick point, never fired because there was nothing to set down. Any program whose return move is triggered by an event has this hole; a fault reset mid-cycle or a dropped bottle opens it too. Make the return depend on the state: empty-handed, standing still, not at the pick point → go home.

XIC(Run)XIC(Axis1:I.Op_Enabled)XIC(Axis1:I.Referenced)XIO(Gripped)XIO(Axis1:I.M oving)XIC(Axis1:I.Motion_Complete)GRT(Axis1:I.Actual_Pos,200)ONS(Park_ONS) [MOV(1,Axis1:O.Record_No),OTL(Axis1:O.Start)]; HOW THIS RUNG WORKS In words. When Run is on, Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on, Axis1:I.Referenced is on, Gripped is off, Axis1:I.Moving is off, Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on, Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is greater than 200 and it is the first scan they are true (the one-shot, remembered in Park_ONS), the rung puts 1 into Axis1:O.Record_No and latches Axis1:O.Start on. Left to right: 1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on. 2. XIC(Axis1:I.Op_Enabled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on. 3. XIC(Axis1:I.Referenced) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Referenced is on. 4. XIO(Gripped) Examine If Open asks: true when Gripped is off. 5. XIO(Axis1:I.Moving) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Moving is off. 6. XIC(Axis1:I.Motion_Complete) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on. 7. GRT(Axis1:I.Actual_Pos,200) Greater Than asks: true when Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is greater than 200. 8. ONS(Park_ONS) One Shot asks: true when it is the first scan they are true (the one-shot, remembered in Park_ONS). 9. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work. Path 1 1. MOV(1,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 1 into Axis1:O.Record_No. Path 2 1. OTL(Axis1:O.Start) Output Latch does: latches Axis1:O.Start on. Why it is built this way: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan. A latch: it stays on until an OTU clears it.

Two questions this rung raised, worth answering here. What unlatches Record_No? Nothing, and nothing needs to: it is not a bit, it is a number the drive samples once, on the rising edge of Start. The value left in it afterwards means nothing until the next Start, and the next Start’s own MOV writes what that move wants. The latch in this rung is Start, and the Start_Ack / Fault rung drops it. Does the ONS fire only once, ever? Once per rising edge of the rung condition. The conditions go true when the carriage is stranded, one pulse, the move starts, Moving makes the rung false, the ONS re-arms; at the pick point GRT is false and nothing fires; the next time something strands the carriage the rung rises again and it fires again. Without the ONS the rung would stay true for the several scans before the drive reports Moving, re-latch Start each scan after Start_Ack dropped it, and the drive would log a double start.

By hand, meanwhile: Toggle on Axis1:O.Jog_Neg (Tags tab, pick the tag, Toggle on the toolbar) jogs the carriage back at the jog speed and stops it at the stroke end; toggle it off there. Jog works for this because no rung writes it. Toggling Home does not: the auto-home rung is an OTE that writes Home false every scan, so the drive never sees the edge. A tag a rung writes is the rung’s, not yours.

The in-position rung is true everywhere

A LIM with its High Limit still 0: Low 149500, High 0. With High below Low, LIM tests outside the band, so the rung was true at every position except 0 to 1495 mm, nearly the opposite of the window wanted. Fill both limits before you trust a LIM, and read the rung’s power flow against the position display once: it should be true in exactly one place.

The record rung asks for a different box every time

A three-position selector gives the controller two inputs, Left and Right; the middle position is both of them off, which is why the middle branch is two XIOs. The RECORD rung is one rung with three branches, one per position, each a MOV into Record_No; built one branch at a time it is one of three, and the guide’s card used to name only the first missing box, so it seemed to want something different each time a branch changed. It now lists everything missing with a count.

The handshake rung that stuck

Covered under the guided track: a Start the drive refuses gets a fault, not a Start_Ack, so an unlatch rung that waits only for Start_Ack leaves Start high, and the first Go after Reset is no edge. The fault branch in [XIC(Axis1:I.Start_Ack),XIC(Axis1:I.Fault)]OTU(Axis1:O.Start) is the fix, and a latch needs a way out for every way in.

Strict or inclusive

LES(Axis1:I.Actual_Pos,200) against the reference’s LEQ: on a measured word the two differ by one count of one hundredth of a millimetre, and the guide accepts either. On a counter or a step word it does not, because GRT(Pick_Count,16) and GEQ(Pick_Count,16) are different programs, and that difference is exactly the kind of bug a compare hides.

Watch for: the bit that is not where it should be

Keep the healthy table in your head and read the status bytes against it. Op_Enabled 0 with Enabled 1: Stop or Halt is low, look at your Power rung’s conditions. Load_Voltage 0: the motor supply is off, the safety circuit or a contactor, not the program. FCT_Control 1: somebody has the configuration tool connected. Referenced 0 with Motion_Complete 1: not homed; the next Start will fault. Warning 1: a Start was ignored, usually a double start, look for a missing Moving or Motion_Complete contact. Fault 1: open the axis in the Device Monitor, the log names the fault, Reset clears it on the rising edge and nothing else does.

Direct mode, jog and teach

Records are the production way: the positions live in the drive and the PLC picks a number. FHPP also has Direct mode: set Axis1:O.OPM1 to 1, write the target into Setpoint_Pos (0.01 mm) and the speed into Setpoint_Vel (percent), and Start runs to it; Record_No then carries the control byte, where bit 0 makes the target relative to where the axis is. Jog_Pos and Jog_Neg move while held, at the jog speed, and stop at the ends of the stroke. Teach writes the actual position into the selected record, Teach_Ack answers, and the record list in the part’s properties changes: that is how positions are set up on a real machine, by jogging to the spot and teaching it.

Try it: jog and teach

Add two push buttons, Jog_P and Jog_N, and a Teach_PB; add rungs XIC(Jog_P_Pressed)OTE(Axis1:O.Jog_Pos);, XIC(Jog_N_Pressed)OTE(Axis1:O.Jog_Neg); and XIC(Teach_PB_Pressed)OTE(Axis1:O.Teach);. Jog to 1500 mm with the selector in the middle, press Teach, and look at the axis properties: record 2 now reads 1500@80. Go runs there from now on.

Level 13 puts a vacuum gripper on this carriage (the part’s Gripper option): pick from a belt, set down at one of three bins by record, and the score watches for moves without a reference, double starts and the wrong bin.

Guided: servo axis

Watch For

Each lesson checks its own routine. A rung that does the lesson’s job but was typed into the lesson before (the fault lamp rung in A2_Move, say, when the lesson is A3_Reset) is still found: the card says where it is and offers Move it. Take the move: a rung left in both places puts two coils on one tag.

the handshake above is also a guided track, the run-up to Level 13: Guided → New Guided Project: Servo Axis. The scene is a small pick cell, the axis with its gripper standing over the end of a short belt, a hopper, the pick eye, a bin at 1500 mm, and a panel with the power selector, Hold, Home, Go, Reset, a record selector, Grip, the fault lamp, two in-position lamps and the position display. The guide panel takes it one routine at a time and checks each lesson while you run it, the way the bottle-line track does: the rungs you write are verified against the reference by their logic, and proven the first time they go true in Run.

Watch for: a latch that never drops

The first version of the handshake rung dropped Start only on Start_Ack. A Start the drive refuses, because the axis is not referenced, gets no acknowledge; it gets a fault. Start then sat high, and after Reset and Home the first Go was no rising edge: the drive saw Start already on and did nothing, and the cell looked dead until somebody pressed Go a second time. The fault branch in the unlatch rung is the fix, and it is in the sandbox program and Level 13’s reference as well now. A latch needs a way out for every way in.

Two things the sim does when you add rungs from the guide: it restarts the machine, so the drive comes up clean and unreferenced (Home again), and it puts the selector back. Both are what a download does to a real cell.

Watch for: a rung typed while online

If you type a lesson’s rung with the controller in Run, it is an online edit: a pending (i) rung that is in the controller but not running until it is accepted and assembled, exactly as in Logix Designer. The card will tell you (’1 online edit in A4_Home not running yet’) and its button assembles it; or go to Program and back to Run, which is a download. The symptom, if you miss it, is a rung that verifies and does nothing: a Home that never fires, and every Go faulting with positioning before homing. Rungs the guide adds for you go straight in.

The vacuum cup at work

the gripper shows what its vacuum is doing. With Grip on, the vacuum builds in about a fifth of a second: the cup’s bellows squash and the ring turns blue; while there is nothing under it, suction rings run inward, which on a real cell is the hiss of a cup pulling air. A held part shows the cup’s seal on its top. When Grip drops the cup gives a short blow-off puff and the part is set down. With the vacuum fault injected the cup stays grey however long Grip is on: that is the picture of Grip 1, Gripped 0.

Machine faults on the servo axis

Tools → Inject Machine Fault… lists the faults that belong to the parts on this floor. Each has a fault card: the symptom, what to watch in the I/O to confirm it, the repair, and what a program should do about it. Repair on an active fault removes its cause the way a technician would; whether the machine runs again is up to the program. The axis also carries the belts’ and the eyes’ faults when the cell has them.

FaultWatchRepairThe program should
Servo axis: load voltage lost
The safety contactor in front of the drive
opens: the logic supply stays, the power
stage loses its load voltage. A move in
progress faults.Load_Voltage 0, Op_Enabled 0, with Enable 1.Close the safety contactor (Repair).Op_Enabled lost while Axis_On is on stops the cycle and lights the fault lamp; after Repair, Reset and Home again.

The mechanics are blocked: every move
faults a moment after it starts.Fault 1 a moment into every move; the log says following error.Free the mechanics (Repair), then Reset.Fault stops the cycle and lights the fault lamp; Reset pulses the drive’s Reset; the axis is homed again before the next pick.

No vacuum at the cup: Grip does nothing
and a held part drops.Grip 1, Part_Below 1, Gripped 0.Clear the vacuum line (Repair).Grip on and no Gripped within half a second: release, retry once, then alarm.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: POWER: with Axis_On, Enable the drive (CCON.B0), hold Stop high (CCON.B1: operation enabled) and Halt high (CPOS.B0: run). Hold_PB is a normally-closed maintained button: press it and Halt drops, so a move pauses where it is; press it again and Halt returns. Op_Enabled comes on with this rung.

pred.q: Axis_On_Pos2 is on and Hold_PB_Pressed is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: Power reaches only part of the rung: Axis1:O.Enable is on, Axis1:O.Stop is on and Axis1:O.Halt is off.

rungs.words: When Axis_On_Pos2 (Axis_On Pos2: 1 in the right-hand position) is on, each path is tested on its own: it turns Axis1:O.Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false); it turns Axis1:O.Stop on (and off whenever the rung is false); if Hold_PB_Pressed (Hold_PB Pressed: NC contact: 1 until pressed) is on, it turns Axis1:O.Halt on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Axis_On_Pos2) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis_On_Pos2 is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Axis1:O.Enable) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Axis1:O.Stop) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Stop on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Hold_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold_PB_Pressed is on.
    2. OTE(Axis1:O.Halt) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Halt on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: RESET: a fault (Fault on, Op_Enabled off, the axis stopped) clears only on the rising edge of Reset (CCON.B3). Reset does nothing else.
rungs.words: When Reset_PB_Pressed (Reset_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on, the rung turns Axis1:O.Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. OTE(Axis1:O.Reset) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2

pred.q: Axis1:I.Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fault_Lamp_On is off. It stops at XIC(Axis1:I.Fault).

rungs.words: When Axis1:I.Fault is on, the rung turns Fault_Lamp_On (Fault_Lamp On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Axis1:I.Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Fault_Lamp_On) Output Energize does: turns Fault_Lamp_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: HOME: Home (CPOS.B2) starts the reference run, the only move the drive allows before the axis is referenced. The axis runs to the home switch at the homing speed, sets position 0 and raises Referenced (SPOS.B7) and Motion_Complete.
rungs.words: When Home_PB_Pressed (Home_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on, Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on and Axis1:I.Moving is off, the rung turns Axis1:O.Home on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Home_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Home_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. XIC(Axis1:I.Op_Enabled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on.
  3. XIO(Axis1:I.Moving) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Moving is off.
  4. OTE(Axis1:O.Home) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Home on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: RECORD: the selector picks the record to run, 1, 2 or 3 (200 mm at 50 %, 1000 mm at 80 %, 1800 mm at 100 % of the maximum velocity). The record is read when Start rises.

pred.q: Rec_Sel_Left is off and Rec_Sel_Right is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: Power reaches only part of the rung: Axis1:O.Record_No is not written (it keeps its value), Axis1:O.Record_No is not written (it keeps its value) and Axis1:O.Record_No is written.

rungs.words: Each path is tested on its own: if Rec_Sel_Left (Rec_Sel Left: 1 in the left position) is on, it puts 1 into Axis1:O.Record_No; if Rec_Sel_Left is off and Rec_Sel_Right (Rec_Sel Right: 1 in the right position) is off, it puts 2 into Axis1:O.Record_No; if Rec_Sel_Right is on, it puts 3 into Axis1:O.Record_No.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Rec_Sel_Left) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rec_Sel_Left is on.
    2. MOV(1,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 1 into Axis1:O.Record_No. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Rec_Sel_Left) Examine If Open asks: true when Rec_Sel_Left is off.
    2. XIO(Rec_Sel_Right) Examine If Open asks: true when Rec_Sel_Right is off.
    3. MOV(2,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 2 into Axis1:O.Record_No. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Rec_Sel_Right) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rec_Sel_Right is on.
    2. MOV(3,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 3 into Axis1:O.Record_No. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: START: on Go, if the axis is referenced and not moving, latch Start (CPOS.B1), through a one-shot on Go_ONS just before the latch, so holding Go gives one Start. The Moving check is what keeps a double start out: a Start while a move runs is ignored by the drive with Warning. Motion_Complete drops at once and returns when the axis is in position.
rungs.words: When Go_PB_Pressed (Go_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on, Axis1:I.Referenced is on, Axis1:I.Moving is off and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Axis1:O.Start on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Go_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Go_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. XIC(Axis1:I.Referenced) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Referenced is on.
  3. XIO(Axis1:I.Moving) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Moving is off.
  4. ONS(Go_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Go_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. OTL(Axis1:O.Start) Output Latch does: latches Axis1:O.Start on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Axis1:O.Start stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: The handshake: the drive answers a Start with Start_Ack (SPOS.B1); drop Start then, so the next Go is a new rising edge. A refused Start (a fault) drops it too, so the first Go after Reset is a fresh edge.

pred.q: Axis1:I.Start_Ack is off and Axis1:I.Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Axis1:O.Start is left as it was. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When either (Axis1:I.Start_Ack is on) or (Axis1:I.Fault is on), the rung unlatches Axis1:O.Start.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Axis1:I.Start_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Start_Ack is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Axis1:I.Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Fault is on.
  2. OTU(Axis1:O.Start) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Axis1:O.Start. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Axis1:O.Start when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.
